title: Where a Plant's Mass Comes From

scenes.visual: A willow in a pot, start and five years later; soil barely changes; the question appears
scenes.tts: In the sixteen hundreds, a man planted a willow stem in a pot of dried soil. The stem weighed five pounds. The soil weighed two hundred pounds. Five years later, he reported a tree of about one hundred sixty nine pounds. The soil was only about two ounces lighter. So where does a plant's mass come from? And how does sunlight end up stored in sugar?
scenes.narration: In the sixteen hundreds, a man planted a willow stem in a pot of dried soil. The stem weighed five pounds. The soil weighed two hundred pounds. Five years later, he reported a tree of about one hundred sixty nine pounds. The soil was only about two ounces lighter. So where does a plant's mass come from? scenes.visual: Photosynthesis as an equation: inputs chips turn into outputs chips
scenes.tts: The answer starts with photosynthesis. Plants, algae and cyanobacteria use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar. They release oxygen. The sugar is glucose, a small sugar molecule with six carbon atoms. With formulas: six carbon dioxide plus six water plus light energy makes one glucose plus six oxygen molecules.

scenes.visual: Atom counts left and right as equal bars: carbon 6, hydrogen 12, oxygen 18
scenes.tts: Count the atoms. On the left, there are six carbon, twelve hydrogen and eighteen oxygen atoms. On the right, there are exactly the same. This is conservation of matter. In a chemical change, atoms are rearranged, never created or destroyed.

scenes.visual: The tree again: carbon dioxide from air and water flow in; soil gives water and minerals
scenes.tts: Now the willow makes sense. The carbon and much of the oxygen in its sugar came from carbon dioxide in the air. The hydrogen came from water. The soil gave water and a small amount of minerals, so the dried soil barely changed. He weighed the tree alive, so part of its gain was water. Most of a plant's dry mass, the mass left after drying, is built from carbon taken in as carbon dioxide.

scenes.visual: A leaf cell with a chloroplast; light absorbed by chlorophyll; glucose made, oxygen released
scenes.tts: In plants and algae, photosynthesis happens in the chloroplast, a green organelle in leaf cells. Inside it, stacks of membranes hold chlorophyll. Chlorophyll is a green pigment that absorbs light, mostly red and blue. That captured energy powers the reactions that split water and build glucose. The oxygen released comes from the split water.

scenes.visual: Energy levels in this sketch: light energy becomes chemical energy in glucose; closing answer
scenes.tts: Energy is conserved too. Light energy is not used up or made. It is transformed into chemical energy, energy held in the arrangement of atoms in molecules. Glucose and oxygen together hold more chemical energy than the carbon dioxide and water they came from. So a plant's dry mass comes mostly from carbon dioxide in the air, and sunlight is stored as chemical energy in sugar.
